correctness.rationale: Polar coordinates and nearest supporting normals give the exact radial function. Counting uncovered arcs in n angular gaps and taking independent m-th powers gives the exact survival law. Jensen on positive parts proves sharp minimization, with strictness immediately above the minimum gap. Two distinct linear slopes at that first knot and one-sided Laplace integrals yield the exact exponential coefficient; strict monotonicity controls the remainder. The beta formula proves universal inverse-power coefficients. All parameters and boundary cases are handled: integer n≥3, integer m≥1, Δ_i∈(0,π), ΣΔ_i=2π; regular polygons are excluded only from the positive excess asymptotic. The finite verifier checks independent polygon areas and asymptotic ratios but is not the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Comparisons were made at the statement-and-implication level, not merely by titles. Buck–Siddon contains deterministic tangency area constructions; Fodor–Hug–Ziebarth samples independent individual supporting halfspaces, not independent rotations of whole polygons; the accessible rotation-intersection sources supply high-dimensional bounds or side counts, not our exact all-m angular-void integral or exponential nonregular correction. Publication search and the corresponding published mathematical-record searches gave no equivalent assertion. Residual risk persists from the unavailable full Brazitikos–Stavrakakis article and possible unindexed one-dimensional coverage formulas.
residual_risks: The full text of the mathematically adjacent rotation-intersection paper by Brazitikos and Stavrakakis was not accessible for a complete line-by-line exclusion; the abstract and paper scope are known.

A general one-dimensional periodic-arc avoidance inequality, possibly published in a different vocabulary, might subsume part of the angular-gap argument; exact implication and the exponential prefactor were separately searched but cannot be universally excluded.
Publication indexing and published mathematical-record search cannot exclude all unindexed or unpublished prior work.

value.rationale: The model preserves n full side-normal clusters under each random rotation, creating highly correlated tangent-line samples. A natural geometric performance measure—the expected area remaining after repeated independent orientations—admits a complete strict optimal-shape classification. The asymptotic error is nonperturbatively exponentially small but contains a sharply recoverable geometric fingerprint: shortest adjacent tangent-normal angle and its multiplicity. This supplies mathematically motivated geometry beyond a low-order moment or arbitrary numerical table. The all-orders universality shows why ordinary asymptotic expansions cannot distinguish initial shapes, while the exact exponential scale can.
